summary: In Greek mythology, Aretus (Ancient Greek Ἄρητος) is a name shared by several figures. The atlas node aretus-nestor is the Pylian prince — son of Nestor and Eurydice (or Anaxibia) — one of the brothers who come forth with their father when Telemachus visits sandy Pylos for the dawn sacrifice to Athena.

sections.heading: Son of Nestor at Pylos
paragraphs: Homer names Aretus among Nestor's sons in the Odyssey when the old king leads the sacrifice at dawn; Apollodorus lists him with Thrasymedes, Pisidice, Polycaste, Perseus, Stratichus, Peisistratus, Echephron, and Antilochus. He is a household presence in the Telemachy rather than a battlefield protagonist.
Homonym care: not Aretus son of Bias and Pero; not Priam's Trojan son slain by Automedon; not the Bebrycian who binds Amycus' gauntlets. The atlas id is Nestor's Pylian son alone.
